name: Survivorship bias measurement

result: survivors-only universe overstates long-only CAGR by +1.2 pp/yr (EW), +1.5 (12-1 momentum), +2.4 (5d losers), +5.5 (top-decile volatility); 18% of the daily liquid universe later delisted; 1,871 delistings (645 distressed) in panel v3. Lower bound: reused-ticker delisted companies still missing.
next_action: recover reused-ticker delisted companies via asof queries and re-measure

name: Realised-vol forecast beats implied vol
hypothesis: QuantLab's forecast of realised movement is more accurate than ATM IV, and the error predicts straddle returns
result: PART 49 ANSWER: in liquid options IV forecasts 1-month realised vol better than QuantLab (OOS log-var MSE 0.085 vs 0.120; VAL 0.069 vs 0.089); QuantLab adds little beyond IV (encompassing coef 0.13, Driscoll-Kraay t 3.9 OOS; t 1.4 VAL); forecast beats only illiquid options' IV. Two-way test: high move+low IV long straddle -2.0%/trade (liquid OOS, t -0.5); high move+high IV capped iron fly -4.8% (t -2.4). First run's 'beyond IV t 12.7 in liquid options' was wrong (week clustering + contaminated joins).
next_action: use the forecast for risk, not to trade options; only revisit with a mid-fill execution test

name: IV vs RV / variance risk premium (Goyal-Saretto)
hypothesis: Straddles on stocks with HV>>IV beat straddles with HV<<IV
result: HV-IV deciles: realistic L/S (long top at ask, short bottom at bid) OOS -22.0% (all, t -12.6), -4.6% (liquid, t -2.6); liquid deciles flat OOS; first-run TRAIN spread +22% was partly wrong-company joins (corrected +9%).
next_action: retire at quoted spreads; only an execution (mid-fill) test could revisit

name: Short-term reversal matrix

next_action: retire as a stand-alone strategy; a regime-conditional (high-volatility) version only if pre-registered
